120	Many of them — there's already a big drift among all the young people, no one there is religious anymore, but
121	they still go to church.
122	So the nations, they all knew that HaShem is the Almighty.
123	So why didn't they go convert?
124	One converted: "And Yitro, priest of Midian, Moshe's father-in-law, heard."
125	He heard and went to convert.
126	Because it's easier to remain a gentile.
127	A slave of ownerless freedom — that suits him fine.
128	The slave prefers that it be easy for him.
129	What do I need now?
130	Six hundred and thirteen mitzvot?
131	Who needs the headaches?
132	Let's stay with the seven Noahide mitzvot.
133	Page 56, tractate Sanhedrin.
134	The Gemara says: the seven Noahide mitzvot.
135	Aleph, bet, gimel, dalet, and "gea'sh."
136	"Gea'sh," an acronym: gilui arayot, avodah zarah, shefichut damim.
137	These are forbidden to them.
138	Aleph, bet, gimel, dalet: aleph, a limb from a living animal.
139	Bet, blessing of HaShem, meaning cursing — they are forbidden to curse HaShem. Gimel, theft. Dalet, judges.
140	They must appoint judges over themselves, so there is an orderly society where people don't swallow each other alive.
141	So these are the seven mitzvot.
142	Is it easier to remain a gentile than to be a Jew?
143	They don't even do these.
144	But idolatry today, they don't really believe in it.
145	For what did Yitro merit?
146	They exalted him.
147	I told you several times that his children sat in the Chamber of Hewn Stone, in the Beit HaMikdash, and Yitro merited
148	that his children, his descendants, were judges in Israel.
149	Do you know what a merit that was for Yitro?
150	So it's clear to me why he merited a Parashah in his name.
151	Noach — it's clear to me why Noach merited a Parashah in his name.
152	"He was a righteous man, perfect in his generations; Noach walked with Elokim."
153	Everyone else was wicked.
154	No one believed him.
155	Now, 120 years does it take to build an ark?
156	What's the problem with raising an ark?
157	Tick-tock, with the Explicit Name, like Moshe Rabbeinu, he could have said a Name and the ark would be lifted.
158	Why did it take so long, 120 years, to build an ark?
159	Rather, it was to bring them back in repentance.
